章節導讀 擬交感神經藥物通过直接激活或間接促進腎上腺素受體作用，本章涵蓋Epinephrine、Norepinephrine、Isoproterenol、Phenylephrine、Albuterol 等重要藥物，以及Dopamine 與Ephedrine 等混合作用型藥物。
交感神經系統的生理角色 交感神經系統在維持血壓中扮演關鍵角色。站立時，压力感受器反射需要交感神經系統維持血管張力與心輸出量。
擬交感神經藥物的分類 分類 作用機制 代表藥物 直接作用型激動劑 直接結合並激活 α 或 β 受體 Epinephrine、Norepinephrine、Phenylephrine 間接作用型 促進內源性兒茶酚胺釋放 Tyramine、Amphetamine 再攝取抑制劑 抑制 NE 的神經再攝取 Cocaine、Tricyclic antidepressants 混合作用型 直接 + 間接作用 Dopamine、Ephedrine 直接作用型 α-受體激動劑 α1 激動劑 藥物 臨床用途 副作用 Phenylephrine 鼻充血、散瞳、維持血壓 血壓過度升高、心搏過緩（反射性） Methoxamine 過去用於維持血壓 血壓過度升高 α1 激活導致血管收縮，血壓升高；反射性心搏過緩是常見副作用
α2 激動劑 藥物 說明 Clonidine 中樞性 α2 激動劑，減少交感輸出；用於高血壓 直接作用型 β-受體激動劑 β1 激動劑 藥物 說明 Dopamine 低劑量作用於 D1；中等劑量 β1；高劑量 α1；用於休克時的正性肌力支持 Dobutamine 主要 β1 agonism；用於急性心衰竭時增加心輸出量 β2 激動劑 藥物 臨床用途 副作用 Albuterol 氣喘、支氣管痙攣 顫抖、心悸 Salbutamol 支氣管擴張 顫抖 Terbutaline 氣喘、子宮鬆弛（安胎） Epinephrine 與 Norepinephrine Epinephrine（EPI） 特性 說明 受體光譜 α1, α2, β1, β2 激動劑 臨床用途 過敏性休克、心臟停止、氣管痙攣 給藥途徑 IM（過敏性休克首選）、SC、IV Norepinephrine（NE） 特性 說明 受體光譜 α1, α2, β1 agonist（無 β2 作用） 臨床用途 敗血性休克低血壓 副作用 組織壞死（外滲時）、心搏過緩 Isoproterenol 特性 說明 受體光譜 β1, β2 agonist（非選擇性 β） 臨床用途 心臟傳導阻斷、bradycardia 副作用 心悸、心律不整 Dopamine Dopamine 的作用呈劑量依賴性：
劑量範圍 主要作用受體 效應 低（< 5 μg/kg/min） D1 腎與腸繫膜血管擴張 中（5-15 μg/kg/min） β1 正性變時/變力 高（> 15 μg/kg/min） α1 血管收縮 間接作用型擬交感神經藥物 藥物 機轉 說明 Tyramine 促進 NE 從儲存囊泡釋放 對 MAO 抑制劑使用者有危險（酪胺危機） Amphetamine 促進 NE/DA 釋放 + 抑制再攝取 CNS 刺激作用 Cocaine 抑制 NE 再攝取（uptake 1） 局部麻醉劑 ##Ephedrine
Ephedrine 具有混合作用機制：
直接作用：α, β agonist 間接作用：促進 NE 釋放 交感神經末梢攝取 NE 的競爭抑制 特性 說明 臨床用途 鼻充血、血壓維持（過去） 特點 口服有效；不易被 MAO 代謝 副作用 中樞刺激、血壓升高、心悸 臨床應用 過敏性休克 Epinephrine（IM）是首選治療：
作用 受體 血管收縮 α1 → 對抗低血壓 支氣管擴張 β2 增加心輸出量 β1 減少肥大細胞脫顆粒 β2 心源性休克 藥物選擇 說明 Dopamine 或 Dobutamine 增加心輸出量 Norepinephrine 必要時維持血壓 敗血性休克 Norepinephrine 是首選升壓劑：
Vasopressin 也常用於膿毒症休克
氣喘/支氣管痙攣 Albuterol（β2 agonist）是首選短效支氣管擴張劑。

章節導讀 抗高血壓藥物是心血管藥理的核心，本章涵蓋α受體阻斷劑（Prazosin 系列）與β受體阻斷劑（Propranolol、Metoprolol）的藥理特性，並涵蓋嗜鉻細胞瘤、高血壓、心絞痛、心衰竭與青光眼的臨床應用。
α-腎上腺素受體阻斷劑 分類與選擇性 藥物 受體選擇性 Phenoxybenzamine α1 > α2（不可逆） Phentolamine α1 = α2（可逆） Prazosin, Terazosin, Doxazosin α1 » α2（可逆） Tamsulosin α1A > α1B, α1D Yohimbine α2 » α1 Phenoxybenzamine 特性 說明 機轉 共價鍵結合 α 受體，不可逆阻斷 作用時間 14-48 小時 主要臨床用途 嗜鉻細胞瘤術前準備 副作用 姿勢性低血壓、心搏過速、鼻塞、射精抑制 注意：嗜鉻細胞瘤患者在 α 阻斷建立前禁止使用 β 阻斷劑
Phentolamine 特性 說明 機轉 競爭性 α1 = α2 阻斷 臨床用途 嗜鉻細胞瘤高血壓危象 心臟刺激作用可能導致心搏過速、心律不整、心肌缺血
Prazosin 系列（α1 選擇性阻斷劑） 藥物 半衰期 特性 Prazosin ~3 小時 需每日多次給藥 Terazosin 9-12 小時 可每日一次 Doxazosin ~22 小時 可每日一次 Tamsulosin 9-15 小時 α1A 高度選擇；對前列腺作用 > 對血管作用 共同臨床用途 說明 高血壓 血管擴張 良性前列腺增生（BPH） 放鬆前列腺/膀胱頸平滑肌 首劑效應（First-dose phenomenon）：初次給藥後可能發生姿勢性低血壓，建議首次劑量在睡前給予。
β-腎上腺素受體阻斷劑 分類 分類 代表藥物 β1 選擇性 非選擇性 Propranolol、Timolol、Nadolol 無 β1 選擇性 Metoprolol、Atenolol、 Bisoprolol 高 混合作用 Labetalol、Carvedilol α1 + β1, β2 受體選擇性 藥物 β1 β2 Propranolol +++ +++ Metoprolol +++ ± Atenolol +++ ± Propranolol 特性 說明 受體 非選擇性 β 阻斷 生體可用率 低且劑量依賴（首渡效應顯著） 藥物動力學 CYP2D6 代謝（慢代謝者血中濃度顯著較高） 臨床用途 高血壓、心絞痛、心律不整、偏頭痛 藥物動力學參數 參數 Propranolol 半衰期 3.5-6 小時 生體可用率 ~30% 脂溶性 高（易穿透 BBB） β1 選擇性阻斷劑 藥物 半衰期 (h) 生體可用率 特殊特性 Metoprolol 3-4 ~50% CYP2D6 代謝；有心臟選択性 Atenolol 6-9 ~40% 腎排泄；每日一次 Bisoprolol 9-12 ~80% 高 β1 選擇性 Nebivolol 11-30 12-96% 高 β1 選擇性 + NO 介導血管擴張 Labetalol 與 Carvedilol 藥物 受體活性 說明 Labetalol α1 + β1, β2 口服後 β:α 阻斷比 ≈ 3:1 Carvedilol α1 + β1, β2 心衰竭標準治療之一 Esmolol 特性 說明 受體 β1 選擇性 半衰期 ~10 分鐘（RBC 酯酶快速代謝） 給藥方式 IV 輸液 臨床用途 手術中高血壓、室上性心律不整 臨床應用 高血壓 藥物類別 說明 β 阻斷劑 抑制腎素釋放；减少心輸出量 α1 阻斷劑 直接擴張血管 聯合治療 通常與利尿劑或血管擴張劑合用 β 阻斷劑對老年人與非裔美國人效果較差
嗜鉻細胞瘤 階段 藥物 術前準備 Phenoxybenzamine（不可逆 α 阻斷） 術前準備（替代） Prazosin、Doxazosin 高血壓危象 Phentolamine（IV）或 Nitroprusside β 阻斷（α 阻斷建立後） Propranolol（控制心搏過速） 警告：先建立 α 阻斷，再使用 β 阻斷；未阻斷 α 時使用 β 阻斷會導致無對抗的 α 效應（血管強烈收縮）
心絞痛 β 阻斷劑減少心肌氧氣需求（↓ 心率、↓ 收縮力、↓ 血壓）。
心衰竭 Carvedilol、Metoprolol、Bisoprolol 被證明可減少心衰竭死亡率。
青光眼 Timolol（局部β 阻斷）減少房水生成，降低眼壓。

β-lactam 抗生素共同特性
具有 four-membered β-lactam ring 抑制細菌胞壁合成所必需的 transpeptidase（penicillin-binding proteins, PBPs） 對分裂旺盛的細菌具 bactericidal 作用 Penicillins
窄效 Penicillins：Penicillin G、Penicillin V，對 Gram+ 球菌有效 抗葡萄球菌 Penicillins：Nafcillin、Oxacillin，對 β-lactamase 穩定 廣效 Penicillins：Ampicillin、Amoxicillin、Piperacillin，對 Gram- 菌擴展有效 β-lactamase 抑制劑複方：Augmentin（Amoxicillin + Clavulanate） Cephalosporins

All are β-lactam compounds, so named because of their four-membered lactam ring. Chemistry All penicillins have the basic structure shown in Figure 43–1 . A thiazolidine ring (A) is attached to a β-lactam ring (B) that carries a secondary amino group (RNH–). Substituents (R; examples shown in Figure 43–2 ) can be attached to the amino group. Structural integrity of the 6-aminopenicillanic acid nucleus (rings A plus B) is essential for the biologic activity of these compounds. Hydrolysis of the β-lactam ring by bacterial β-lactamases yields penicilloic acid, which lacks antibacterial activity. A. Classification Substituents of the 6-aminopenicillanic acid moiety determine the essential pharmacologic and antibacterial properties of the result- ing molecules. Penicillins can be assigned to one of three groups (below). Within each of these groups are compounds that are rela- tively stable to gastric acid and suitable for oral administration, eg, penicamoxicillin> V, dicloxacillin, and amoxicillin. 792 SECTION VIII Chemotherapeutic Drugs 1600 units per mg (1 unit = 0.6 mcg; 1 million units of penicillin = 0.6 g). Semisynthetic penicillins are prescribed by weight rather than units. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of any penicillin (or other antimicrobial) is usually given in mcg/mL. Most penicillins are formulated as the sodium or potassium salt of the free acid. Potassium penicillin G contains about 1.7 mEq of K + per million units of penicillin (2.8 mEq/g). Nafcillin contains Na + , 2.8 mEq/g. Procaine salts and benzathine salts of penicillin G provide repository forms for intramuscular injection. In dry crystalline form, penicillin salts are stable for years at 4°C. Solutions lose their activity rapidly (eg, 24 hours at 20°C) and must be prepared fresh for administration. Mechanism of Action Penicillins, like all β-lactam antibiotics, inhibit bacterial growth by interfering with the transpeptidation reaction of bacterial cell wall synthesis . The cell wall is a rigid outer layer unique to bacte- rial species. It completely surrounds the cytoplasmic membrane ( Figure 43–3 ), maintains cell shape and integrity, and prevents cell lysis from high osmotic pressure. The cell wall is composed of a complex, cross-linked polymer of polysaccharides and polypeptides, peptidoglycan (also known as murein or mucopep- tide). The polysaccharide contains alternating amino sugars, N -acetylglucosamine and N -acetylmuramic acid ( Figure 43–4 ). A five-amino-acid peptide is linked to the N -acetylmuramic acid sugar. This peptide terminates in D-alanyl-D-alanine. Penicillin- binding protein (PBP, an enzyme) removes the terminal alanine in the process of forming a cross-link with a nearby peptide. Cross- links give the cell wall its structural rigidity. Beta-lactam antibiot- ics, structural analogs of the natural D-Ala-D-Ala substrate, covalently bind to the active site of PBPs. This inhibits the trans- peptidation reaction ( Figure 43–5 ), halting peptidoglycan synthe- sis, and the cell dies. The exact mechanism of cell death is not completely understood, but autolysins and disruption of cell wall morphogenesis are involved. Beta-lactam antibiotics kill bacterial cells only when they are actively growing and synthesizing cell wall. Resistance Resistance to penicillins and other β-lactams is due to one of four general mechanisms: (1) inactivation of antibiotic by β-lactamase, (2) modification of target PBPs, (3) impaired penetration of drug to target PBPs, and (4) efflux. Beta-lactamase production is the most common mechanism of resistance. Hundreds of different β-lactamases have been identified. Some, such as those produced by Staphylococcus aureus, Haemophilus influenzae , and Escherichia coli , β Lactamase PBP Cytoplasmic membrane Periplasmic space Cell wall Peptidoglycan Outer membrane PBP Porin FIGURE 43–3 A highly simplified diagram of the cell envelope of a gram-negative bacterium. The outer membrane, a lipid bilayer, is present in gram-negative but not gram-positive organisms. It is penetrated by porins, proteins that form channels providing hydrophilic access to the cytoplasmic membrane. The peptidoglycan layer is unique to bacteria and is much thicker in gram-positive organisms than in gram- negative ones. Together, the outer membrane and the peptidoglycan layer constitute the cell wall. Penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) are membrane proteins that cross-link peptidoglycan. Beta lactamases, if present, reside in the periplasmic space or on the outer surface of the cytoplasmic membrane, where they may destroy β-lactam antibiotics that penetrate the outer membrane.
CHAPTER 43 Beta-Lactam & Other Cell Wall- & Membrane-Active Antibiotics 793 are relatively narrow in substrate specificity, preferring penicillins to cephalospoβ-lactamase β-lactamases, eg, AmpC β-lactamase pro- duced by Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Enterobacter sp, and extended- spectrum β-lactamases (ESBLs), hydrolyze both cephalosporins and penicillins. Carbapenems are highly resistant to hydrolysis by peni- cillinases and cephalosporinases, but they are hydrolyzed by metallo-β lactamase and carbapenemases. Altered target PBPs are the basis of methicillin resistance in staphylococci and of penicillin resistance in pneumococci and enterococci. These resistant organisms produce PBPs that have low affinity for binding β-lactam antibiotics, and consequently, they are not inhibited except at relatively high, often clinically unachievable, drug concentrations. Resistance due to impaired penetration of antibiotic to target PBPs occurs only in gram-negative species because of their imper- meable outer cell wall membrane, which is absent in gram-positive bacteria. Beta-lactam antibiotics cross the outer membrane and enter gram-negative organisms via outer membrane protein channels called porins. Absence of the proper channel or down- regulation of its production can greatly impair drug entry into the cell. Poor penetration alone is usually not sufficient to confer resistance because enough antibiotic eventually enters the cell to inhibit grβ-lactamaseer, this barrier can become important in the presence of a β-lactamase, even a relatively inactive one, as long as it can hydrolyze drug faster than it enters the cell. Gram-negative organisms also may produce an efflux pump, which consists of cytoplasmic and periplasmic protein components that efficiently transport some β-lactam antibiotics from the periplasm back across the outer membrane. Pharmacokinetics Absorption of orally administered drug differs greatly for different penicillins, depending in part on their acid stability and protein binding. Gastrointestinal absorption of nafcillin is erratic, so it is not suitable for oral administration. Dicloxacillin, ampicillin, and amoxicillin are acid-stable and relatively well absorbed, producing serum concentrations in the range of 4–8 mcg/mL after a 500-mg oral dose. Absorption of most oral penicillins (amoxicillin being an exception) is impaired by food, and the drugs should be admin- istered at least 1–2 hours before or after a meal. Intravenous administration of penicillin G is preferred to the intramuscular route because of irritation and local pain from intra- muscular injection of large doses. Serum concentrations 30 minutes after an intravenous injection of 1 g of a penicillin (equivalent to approximately 1.6 million units of penicillin G) are 20–50 mcg/ mL. Only a small amount of the total drug in serum is present as free drug, the concentration of which is determined by protein binding. Highly protein-bound penicillins (eg, nafcillin) generally achieve lower free-drug concentrations in serum than less protein- bound penicillins (eg, penicillin G or ampicillin). Protein binding becomes clinically relevant when the protein-bound percentage is approximately 95% or more. Penicillins are widely distributed in body fluids and tissues with a few exceptions. They are polar mol- ecules, so intracellular concentrations are well below those found in extracellular fluids. The cell wall of gram- positive bacteria is made up of long peptidoglycan polymer chains consisting of the alternating aminohexoses N -acetylglucosamine (G) and N -acetylmuramic acid (M) with pentapeptide side chains linked (in S aureus ) by pentaglycine bridges. The exact composition of the side chains varies among species. The diagram illustrates small segments of two such polymer chains and their amino acid side chains. These linear polymers must be cross-linked by transpeptida- tion of the side chains at the points indicated by the asterisk to achieve the strength necessary for cell viability. 794 SECTION VIII Chemotherapeutic Drugs Benzathine and procaine penicillins are formulated to delay absorption, resulting in prolonged blood and tissue concentra- tions. A single intramuscular injection of 1.2 million units of benzathine penicillin maintains serum levels above 0.02 mcg/mL for 10 days, sufficient to treat β-hemolytic streptococcal infection. After 3 weeks, levels still exceed 0.003 mcg/mL, which is enough to prevent β-hemolytic streptococcal infection. A 600,000 unit dose of procaine penicillin yields peak concentrations of 1–2 mcg/ mL and clinically useful concentrations for 12–24 hours after a single intramuscular injection. Penicillin concentrations in most tissues are equal to those in serum. Penicillin is also excreted into sputum and milk to levels 3–15% of those in the serum. Penetration into the eye, the prostate, and the central nervous system is poor. However, with active inflammation of the meninges, as in bacterial meningitis, penicillin concentrations of 1–5 mcg/mL can be achieved with a daily par- enteral dose of 18–24 million units. These concentrations are sufficient to kill susceptible strains of pneumococci and meningococci. Penicillin is rapidly excreted by the kidneys; small amounts are excreted by other routes. About 10% of renal excretion is by glomerular filtration and 90% by tubular secretion. The normal half-life of penicillin G is approximately 30 minutes; in renal failure, it may be as long as 10 hours. Ampicillin and the extended- spectrum penicillins are secreted more slowly than penicillin G and have half-lives of 1 hour. For penicillins that are cleared by the kidney, the dose must be adjusted according to renal function, with approximately one fourth to one third the normal dose being administered if creatinine clearance is 10 mL/min or less ( Table 43–1 ). Nafcillin is primarily cleared by biliary excretion. Oxacillin, dicloxacillin, and cloxacillin are eliminated by both the kidney and biliary excretion; no dosage adjustment is required for these drugs in renal failure. Clinical Uses Except for oral amoxicillin, penicillins should be given 1–2 hours before or after a meal; they should not be given with food to minimize binding to food proteins and acid inactivation. Blood levels of all penicillins can be raised by simultaneous administra- tion of probenecid, 0.5 g (10 mg/kg in children) every 6 hours orally, which impairs renal tubular secretion of weak acids such as β-lactam compounds. Penicillins should never be used for viral infections and should be prescribed only when there is reasonable suspicion of, or documented infectio<span stylePenicillinb923c">Penicillinsceptible organisms . A. Penicillinpenicillinn G is a drug of choice for infections caused by streptococci, meningococci, some enterococci, penicillin-susceptible pneumo- cocci, non-β-lactamase-producing staphylococci, Treponema pallidum and certain other spirochetes, Clostridium species, Actinomyces and certain other gram-positive rods, and non-β- lactamase-producing gram-negative anaerobic organisms. Depend- ing on the organism, the site, and the severity of infection, effective doses range between 4 and 24 million units per day administered intravenously in four to six divided doses. High-dose penicillin G can also be given as a continuous intravenous infusion. Penicillin V, the oral form of penicillin, is indicated only in minor infections because of its relatively poor bioavailability, the need for dosing four times a day, and its narrow antibacterial spectrum. Amoxicillin (see below) is often used instead. Benzathine penicillin and procaine penicillin G for intramus- cular injection yield low but prolonged drug levels. A single intra- muscular injection of benzathine penicillin, 1.2 million units, is effective treatment for β-hemolytic streptococcal pharyngitis; given intramuscularly once every 3–4 weeks, it prevents reinfec- tion. Benzathine penicillin G, 2.4 million units intramuscularly once a week for 1–3 weeks, is effective in the treatment of syphilis. Procaine penicillin G, formerly a work horse for treating uncom- plicated pneumococcal pneumonia or gonorrhea, is rarely used now because many strains are penicillin-resistant.

Ampicillin and amoxicillin can cause skin rashes that are not allergic in nature. These rashes frequently occur when aminopenicillins are inappropriately prescribed for a viral illness.
CEPHALOSPORINS & CEPHAMYCINS Cephalosporins are similar to penicillins, but more stable to many bacterial β lactamases and therefore have a broader spectrum of activity. However, strains of E coli and Klebsiella sp expressing extended-spectrum β lactamases that can hydrolyze most cepha- losporins are a growing clinical concern. Cephalosporins are not active against enterococci and L monocytogenes . Chemistry The nucleus of the cephalosporins, 7-aminocephalosporanic acid ( Figure 43–6 ), bears a close resemblance to 6-aminopenicillanic acid ( Figure 43–1 ). The intrinsic antimicrobial activity of natural cephalosporins is low, but the attachment of various R 1 and R 2 groups has yielded hundreds of potent compounds of low toxicity. Cephalosporins can be classified into four major groups or gen- erations, depending mainly on the spectrum of antimicrobial activity.
FIRST-GENERATION CEPHALOSPORINS First-generation cephalosporins include cefazolin, cefadroxil, cephalexin, cephalothin, cephapirin, and cephradine. These drugs are very active against gram-positive cocci, such as pneumo- cocci, streptococci, and staphylococci. Traditional cephalosporins are not active against methicillin-resistant strains of staphylococci; how- ever, new compounds have been developed that have activity against methicillin-resistant strains (see below). E coli, K pneumoniae , and Proteus mirabilis are often sensitive, but activity against P aeruginosa , indole-positive proteus species, Enterobacter sp, S marcescens , Citrobacter sp, and Acinetobacter sp is poor. Anaerobic cocci (eg, peptococci, peptostreptococci) are usually sensitive, but Bacteroides fragilis is not. Pharmacokinetics & Dosage A. Oral Cephalexin, cephradine, and cefadroxil are absorbed from the gut to a variable extent. After oral doses of 500 mg, serum levels are 15–20 mcg/mL. Urine concentration is usually very high, but in most tis- sues levels are variable and generally lower than in serum. Cephalexin and cephradine are given orally in dosages of 0.25–0.5 g four times daily (15–30 mg/kg/d) and cefadroxil in dosages of 0.5–1 g twice daily. Excretion is mainly by glomerular filtration and tubular secre- tion into the urine. Drugs that block tubular secretion, eg, probenecid, may increase serum levels substantially. Parenteral Cefazolin is the only first-generation parenteral cephalosporin still in general use. After an intravenous infusion of 1 g, the peak level of cefazolin is 90–120 mcg/mL. The usual intravenous dosage of cefazolin for adults is 0.5–2 g intravenously every 8 hours. Cefazolin can also be administered intramuscularly. Excretion is via the kidney, and dose adjustments must be made for impaired renal function. Clinical Uses Oral drugs may be used for the treatment of urinary tract infec- tions and staphylococcal or streptococcal infections, including cellulitis or soft tissue abscess. However, oral cephalosporins should not be relied on in serious systemic infections. Cefazolin penetrates well into most tissues. It is a drug of choice for surgical prophylaxis. Cefazolin may also be a choice in infections for which it is the least toxic drug (eg, penicillinase- producing E coli or K pneumoniae ) and in individuals with staphylococcal or streptococcal infections who have a history of penicillin allergy other than immediate hypersensitivity. Cefazolin does not penetrate the central nervous system and cannot be used to treat meningitis. Cefazolin is an altepenicillin</spanpenicillintaphylo- coccal penicillin for patients who are allergic to penicillin.
SECOND-GENERATION CEPHALOSPORINS Members of the second-generation cephalosporins include cefaclor, cefamandole, cefonicid, cefuroxime, cefprozil, loracarbef, and ceforanide; and the structurally related cephamycins cefoxitin, cefmetazole , and cefotetan , which have activity against anaer- obes. This is a heterogeneous group with marked individual differ- ences in activity, pharmacokinetics, and toxicity. In general, they are active against organisms inhibited by first-generation drugs, but in addition they have extended gram-negative coverage. Klebsiella sp (including those resistant to cephalothin) are usually sensitive. Cefamandole, cefuroxime, cefonicid, ceforanide, and cefaclor are active against H influenzae but not against serratia or B fragilis . In contrast, cefoxitin, cefmetazole, and cefotetan are active against B fragilis and some serratia strains but are less active against H influenzae . As with first-generation agents, none is active against enterococci or P aeruginosa . Second-generation cepha- losporins may exhibit in vitro activity against Enterobacter sp., but resistant mutants that constitutively express a chromosomal β lactamase that hydrolyzes these compounds (and third-generation cephalosporins) are readily selected, and they should not be used to treat enterobacter infections. Pharmacokinetics & Dosage A. Oral Cefaclor, cefuroxime axetil, cefprozil, and loracarbef can be given orally. The usual dosage for adults is 10–15 mg/kg/d in two to four divided doses; children should be given 20–40 mg/kg/d up to a maximum of 1 g/d. Except for cefuroxime axetil, these drugs are not predictably active against penicillin-non-susceptible pneumo- cocci and should be used cautiously, if at all, to treat suspected or proved pneumococcal infections. Cefaclor is more susceptible to β-lactamase hydrolysis compared with the other agents, and its usefulness is correspondingly diminished. B. Parenteral After a 1-g intravenous infusion, serum levels are 75–125 mcg/mL for most second-generation cephalosporins. Intramuscular admin- istration is painful and should be avoided. Doses and dosing intervals vary depending on the specific agent ( Table 43–2 ). There are marked differences in half-life, protein binding, and interval between doses. All are renally cleared and require dosage adjust- ment in renal failure. Clinical Uses The oral second-generationβ-lactamaserins are active against β-lactamase-producing H influenzae or Moraxella catarrhalis and have been primarily used to treat sinusitis, otitis, and lower respiratory tract infections, in which these organisms have an important role. Because of their activity against anaerobes (including many B fragilis strains ), cefoxitin, cefotetan, or cefmetazole can be used to treat mixed anaero- bic infections such as peritonitis, diverticulitis, and pelvic inflamma- tory disease. Cefuroxime is usβ-lactamase community-acquired pneumonia because it is active against β-lactamase-producing H inpenicillinr K pneumoniae and some penicillin-non-susceptible pneumococci. Although cefuroxime crosses the blood-brain barrier, it is less effective in treatment of meningitis than ceftriaxone or cefo- taxime and should not be used.

章節導讀

本章節介紹 β-lactam 類與其他作用於細菌細胞壁的抗生素。

β-lactam 抗生素共同特性

  • 具有 four-membered β-lactam ring
  • 抑制細菌胞壁合成所必需的 transpeptidase（penicillin-binding proteins, PBPs）
  • 對分裂旺盛的細菌具 bactericidal 作用

Penicillins

  • 窄效 Penicillins：Penicillin G、Penicillin V，對 Gram+ 球菌有效
  • 抗葡萄球菌 Penicillins：Nafcillin、Oxacillin，對 β-lactamase 穩定
  • 廣效 Penicillins：Ampicillin、Amoxicillin、Piperacillin，對 Gram- 菌擴展有效
  • β-lactamase 抑制劑複方：Augmentin（Amoxicillin + Clavulanate）

Cephalosporins

  • 分為五代，各有抗菌譜特色
  • 第一代（cefazolin）：主要用於 Gram+ 球菌手術預防
  • 第三代（ceftriaxone、ceftazidime）：廣效，涵蓋 Gram- 菌，部分可入腦脊液
  • 第四代（cefepime）：對 β-lactamase 穩定，對 Pseudomonas 有效

Vancomycin

  • 抑制 peptidoglycan 鏈交聯，對 Gram+ 菌有強效 bactericidal 作用
  • 臨床上用於 MRSA、嚴重 Gram+ 菌感染

BETALACTAM COMPOUNDS

PENICILLINS The penicillins share features of chemistry, mechanism of action, pharmacology, and immunologic characteristics with cephalosporins, monobactams, carbapenems, and β-lactamase inhibitors. All are β-lactam compounds, so named because of their four-membered lactam ring. Chemistry All penicillins have the basic structure shown in Figure 43–1 . A thiazolidine ring (A) is attached to a β-lactam ring (B) that carries a secondary amino group (RNH–). Substituents (R; examples shown in Figure 43–2 ) can be attached to the amino group. Structural integrity of the 6-aminopenicillanic acid nucleus (rings A plus B) is essential for the biologic activity of these compounds. Hydrolysis of the β-lactam ring by bacterial β-lactamases yields penicilloic acid, which lacks antibacterial activity. A. Classification Substituents of the 6-aminopenicillanic acid moiety determine the essential pharmacologic and antibacterial properties of the result- ing molecules. Penicillins can be assigned to one of three groups (below). Within each of these groups are compounds that are rela- tively stable to gastric acid and suitable for oral administration, eg, penicamoxicillin> V, dicloxacillin, and amoxicillin. 章節導讀

膽鹼受體激活劑分為直接作用型（直接激活膽鹼受體）與間接作用型（抑制膽鹼酯酶使內源性 ACh 累積）兩大類。本章涵蓋Pilocarpine、Bethanechol、Physostigmine、Neostigmine 等重要藥物，以及Organophosphate 中毒的緊急處理。

膽鹼受體的光譜作用分類

直接作用型膽鹼激動劑

類別 代表藥物 受體選擇性
膽鹼酯類 Acetylcholine、Methacholine、Carbachol、Bethanechol Carbachol（M+N）；Bethanechol（M 選擇性）
天然生物鹼 Muscarine、Pilocarpine、Nicotine Muscarine/Pilocarpine（M 選擇性）；Nicotine（N 選擇性）

間接作用型膽鹼激動劑（抗膽鹼酯酶藥物）

類別 代表藥物 說明
可逆性抑制劑 Physostigmine、Neostigmine、Donepezil、Rivastigmine、Galantamine 暫時抑制 AChE
不可逆性抑制劑 Organophosphates（Parathion、Malathion、Sarin） 與 AChE 形成穩定共價鍵

Muscarinic Agonists

藥物 特性 臨床用途
Pilocarpine 叔胺結構，選擇性 M3 agonist 青光眼（開放房水排出）、乾眼症
Bethanechol 合成膽鹼酯，M 選擇性（膀胱/腸道） 術後尿滯留、神經性膀胱、腸阻塞
Carbachol M + N agonist 青光眼（局部）

Nicotinic Agonists

藥物 特性 臨床用途
Nicotine 煙草生物鹼，低劑量興奮 N_N1，高劑量引起去極化阻斷 戒菸輔助製劑（貼片、口香糖）

Acetylcholinesterase 抑制劑

可逆性抑制劑

藥物 特性 臨床用途 副作用
Physostigmine 叔胺，可穿透 BBB 抗膽鹼藥物中毒、重症肌無力 膽鹼危機
Neostigmine 季銨化合物，不穿透 BBB 重症肌無力、逆轉非去極化 NMJ 阻斷劑 膽鹼危機、心搏過緩

Galantamine AChE 抑制 + nAChR 調控 阿茲海默症 胃腸道症狀

不可逆性抑制劑：Organophosphates

高毒性農藥（Parathion、Malathion）與化學戰劑（Sarin、VX）

Muscarinic 受體拮抗劑 Atropine 及其相關藥物 Atropine 是競爭性 muscarinic 拮抗劑，阻斷所有 M 受體亞型（M1-M5）。
藥物類型 代表藥物 CNS 穿透性 叔胺化合物 Atropine、Scopolamine 高穿透 BBB 季銨化合物 Ipratropium、Glycopyrrolate 不穿透 BBB Atropine 的組織效應 系統 效應 說明 眼睛 散瞳（Mydriasis）、睫狀肌麻痺（Cycloplegia） M3 受體阻斷；可能誘發急性閉角型青光眼 唾液腺 分泌顯著減少 口乾；最敏感的組織之一 心臟 劑量依賴性：低劑量（0.4-0.6 mg）可能引起心搏過緩（阻斷突觸前 M2 自體受體）；中等至高劑量引起心搏過速 支氣管 支氣管擴張、分泌減少 對 COPD 患者顯著 GI 道 蠕動與分泌減少 抗痙攣作用 泌尿道 逼尿肌收縮減少 尿滯留 CNS 高劑量：興奮、譫妄、幻覺 M1 受體阻斷 Scopolamine 特性 說明 與 Atropine 的差異 CNS 作用更強（鎮靜、遺忘作用） 臨床用途 動暈症（經皮貼片）、術前鎮靜 合成 Muscarinic 拮抗劑 藥物 特性 臨床用途 Ipratropium 季銨化合物，不穿透 BBB COPD、氣喘（吸入） Tiotropium 長效 muscarinic 拮抗劑（LAMA） COPD（每日一次） Glycopyrrolate 季銨化合物 術前給藥（止涎）、COPD Tropicamide 短效散瞳劑 眼科散瞳/睫狀肌麻痺 Oxybutynin M3 選擇性 膀胱過動症、尿失禁 Tolterodine M3 選擇性 膀胱過動症 Darifenacin、Solifenacin M3 選擇性，長效 膀胱過動症，每日一次 神經節阻斷劑 藥物 說明 Hexamethonium 競爭性神經節阻斷劑（已停用） Mecamylamine 可穿透 BBB，過去用於高血壓 Trimethaphan 短效神經節阻斷劑，用於高血壓急症 副作用：姿勢性低血壓、便祕、尿滯留、視覺模糊

非去極化型（競爭性拮抗劑） 藥物 作用時間 特性 Rocuronium 中效 快速 onset，適合快速誘導插管 Vecuronium 中效 心臟副作用少，肝臟代謝 Cisatracurium 中效 主要經 Hofmann 降解（非酶性），適合肝腎功能不良患者 Pancuronium 長效 可能引起心搏過速（抗迷走神經作用） 去極化型 藥物 機轉 臨床說明 Succinylcholine 持續激活 N_N2 受體，導致持續去極化 快速 onset，短時間（數分鐘）；禁忌：惡性高熱病史、高血鉀、燒傷/神經損傷 逆轉方法 方法 說明 Neostigmine AChE 抑制劑，增加 NMJ 的 ACh 濃度 Sugammadex 選擇性結合劑，包裹 Rocuronium/Vecuronium Atropine 中毒處理 兒童對 Atropine 極度敏感，2 mg 即可能致命
中毒症狀 口乾、瞳孔散大、心搏過速、皮膚發熱發紅、興奮、譫妄
口訣：「乾如枯骨、盲如蝙蝠、紅如甜菜、瘋如帽商」
治療 方法 說明 支持性療法 降溫毯、癲癇控制（Diazepam） Physostigmine AChE 抑制劑（穿透 BBB），小劑量緩慢 IV（成人 1-4 mg） 禁忌症 禁忌情況 說明 閉角型青光眼 Atropine 可能誘發急性發作 攝護腺肥大 可能誘發尿滯留 GI 阻塞 腸阻塞 麻痹性腸阻塞 — 尿滯留 — 心搏過速性心律不整 — 藥物總整理 藥物 機轉 臨床用途 副作用 Atropine Muscarinic 拮抗劑（M1-M5） 術前給藥、心搏過緩、眼科散瞳、GI 痙攣 口乾、視覺模糊、心搏過速、尿滯留、CNS 興奮 Scopolamine Muscarinic 拮抗劑 動暈症（貼片）、術前鎮靜 嗜睡、視覺模糊、口乾 Ipratropium Muscarinic 拮抗劑（吸入） COPD、氣喘 局部刺激、極少全身作用 Tiotropium 長效 muscarinic 拮抗劑（LAMA） COPD（每日一次） 口乾、便祕 Glycopyrrolate 季銨 muscarinic 拮抗劑 術前給藥（止涎）、COPD 口乾 Tropicamide 短效 muscarinic 拮抗劑 眼科散瞳/睫狀肌麻痺 視覺模糊 Rocuronium 非去極化 NMJ 阻斷劑 麻醉誘導、維持肌肉鬆弛 注射部位疼痛 Vecuronium 非去極化 NMJ 阻斷劑 麻醉維持 肝功能影響 Cisatracurium 非去極化 NMJ 阻斷劑 麻醉（肝腎功能不良患者） 注射部位反應 Succinylcholine 去極化 NMJ 阻斷劑 快速誘導插管、短手術 肌肉疼痛、高血鉀、心律不整、惡性高熱

content:
Development and Regulation of Drugs 章節導讀 藥物開發與法規涵蓋從新藥發現到上市審批的完整歷程，包括藥物篩選、臨床試驗階段、FDA 審批程序，以及孤兒藥與加速審批等特殊機制。
新藥發現流程 藥物標靶的發現 真正的新藥需要發現新的藥物標靶（Drug Target）——即疾病的病理生理過程或受質。多數新標靶發現起源於學術界與政府研究機構。
藥物開發的兩大階段 階段 說明 發現階段 在實驗室中對化合物進行篩選與優化 開發階段 耗時且昂貴的化學、藥理、毒理研究 臨床試驗 臨床試驗階段 階段 目的 受試人數 Phase I 安全性、耐受性、藥物動力學 20-100 健康志願者 Phase II 初步療效、劑量範圍 100-500 患者 Phase III 大規模療效與安全性確認 1000-5000 患者 Phase IV 上市後監視 廣大使用者群 IND 申請 IND（Investigational New Drug）申請：製藥公司向 FDA 申請進行人體臨床試驗。
NDA 申請 NDA（New Drug Application）申請：完成 Phase III 後，向 FDA 提交的上市許可申請。
特殊藥物類型 孤兒藥（Orphan Drugs） 特性 說明 定義 用於治療罕見疾病（美國定義：患者 < 20 萬人）的藥物 激勵措施 市場独占期 7 年、稅收優惠、補助資助 加速審批（Accelerated Approval） 允許根據替代終點（Surrogate Endpoint）提前批准用於治療重大疾病的藥物。
藥物專利與市場独占 類型 說明 專利保護 申請後 20 年独占期 市場独占 NDA 批准後一定期間的市場独占（取決於藥物類型） 學名藥 品牌藥專利過期後的仿製藥 生物製劑與疫苗 生物製劑 特性 說明 定義 由生物來源（如蛋白質、抗體）製成的藥物 審批途徑 BLA（Biologics License Application） 例子 Insulin、Monoclonal antibodies、Erythropoietin 疫苗 疫苗開發需經過特殊的臨床試驗設計，包括免疫原性與保護效力評估。
藥物命名 類型 例子 說明 化學名 N-acetyl-para-aminophenol 藥物的化學結構名稱 非專利名（INN） Acetaminophen 全球通用的官方名稱 商品名 Tylenol 製藥公司的品牌名稱 上市後監視 藥物警戒（Pharmacovigilance） 機制 說明 不良反應通報系統 醫療專業人員與製藥公司向 FDA 通報不良反應 藥物安全警告 FDA 發布 black box warning 或修改仿單 上市後研究 Phase IV 研究補充安全性數據 重要：臨床試驗樣本數有限，罕見不良反應（發生率 < 1/1000）可能在上市後才被發現。
特殊人群的藥物使用 孕婦用藥 分級 說明 A 在對照研究中未顯示風險 B 動物研究無風險，但人類研究不足 C 動物研究顯示風險，人類研究不足 D 有證據顯示風險，但利益大於風險 X 禁忌於孕婦 兒童用藥 兒童並非小型成人——藥物動力學與藥效學與成人有顯著差異。
藥物價格與可近性 問題 說明 藥物開發成本 新藥開發平均耗時 10-15 年，成本可達數十億美元 價格爭議 品牌藥與學名藥價格差異、國際價格差異 學名藥的好處 增加藥物可近性，降低醫療成本 學名藥（Generic Drugs）在品牌藥專利過期後上市，需證明與品牌藥的生體相等性（Bioequivalence）。

content:
Drug Biotransformation 章節導讀 藥物生物轉化是終止親脂性藥物作用的關鍵過程，本章介紹Phase I（氧化還原水解）與Phase II（結合反應）兩大代谢途径，以及Cytochrome P450系統與藥物基因體學的臨床重要性。
為何需要藥物生物轉化 Paracelsus 原則：「劑量決定毒性」
親脂性藥物若僅靠腎臟排泄，會因為腎小管遠端被動擴散回血液而作用時間過長。肝臟代謝將親脂性藥物轉化為更親水性的代謝物以便排泄。
藥物 若不經代謝 實際半衰期 Thiopental 可能達數天 8-12 小時（經肝代謝） Phase I 反應：氧化、還原、水解 Cytochrome P450 系統 Cytochrome P450（CYP）是肝臟微粒體中最主要的藥物代謝酶系統：
CYP 酶 臨床相關性 臨床例子 CYP3A4 約佔 30% 臨床相關代謝 Ketoconazole、Erythromycin、Midazolam CYP2C9 約佔 20% Warfarin、Phenytoin CYP1A2 約佔 15% Caffeine、Theophylline CYP2D6 約佔 5% Codeine（需轉化為 morphine）、Metoprolol、Propranolol CYP2C19 重要 Omeprazole、Clopidogrel（活化） 主要 Phase I 反應類型 反應類型 例子 芳香烴羥化 Phenytoin、Warfarin 脂肪烴羥化 Pentobarbital N-去烷基化 Morphine、Caffeine S-氧化 Thioridazine 水解 Succinylcholine（膽鹼酯酶） Phase II 反應：結合反應 Phase II 反應將內源性底物與藥物或其 Phase I 代謝物結合，產生高極性、易排泄的產物。

Drug Receptors and Pharmacodynamics 章節導讀 藥效學研究藥物如何通過與受體結合產生作用，本章深入探討受體-效應器耦合、備用受體、競爭性與非競爭性拮抗等核心概念，並介紹部分激動劑與反向激動劑等特殊藥物類型。
受體的分子本質 受體的分類 藥物受體（Receptor）大多是蛋白質分子，根據結構與訊號傳導機制分為：
受體類型 例子 訊號機制 調節型受體 GPCR（G 蛋白偶聯受體） 透過 G 蛋白激活下游效應酶 離子通道型受體 nAChR、GABA_A 受體 直接控制離子流動 酪氨酸激酶受體 胰島素受體、EGF 受體 激活細胞內酪氨酸激酶活性 核內受體 類固醇、甲狀腺素受體 調節基因轉錄 藥物濃度-效應關係 濃度-效應曲線 在理想化系統中，藥物濃度與效應呈雙曲線關係：
E = E _ m a x × C / ( E C _ 5 0 + C ) E：在濃度 C 時觀察到的效應 E_max：藥物可產生的最大效應 EC_50：產生 50% 最大效應的藥物濃度 效應與劑量對數曲線 將效應對濃度對數作圖，雙曲線轉化為S 形曲線，擴展低濃度端的刻度而壓縮高濃度端。
受體結合 藥物與受體的結合關係：
B = B _ m a x × C / ( K _ d + C ) B_max：受體總濃度 K_d：解離常數 — K_d 越低，代表受體對藥物的親和力越高 EC_50 與 K_d：兩者可以相同或不同，取決於受體-效應器耦合效率 受體-效應器耦合與備用受體 耦合機制 藥物佔據受體後需要經過耦合（Coupling）過程才能產生藥理效應。耦合效率決定相同受體佔據程度下的效應強度差異。
備用受體（Spare Receptors） 備用受體現象說明：即使 agonist 濃度不足以佔據全部受體，仍可達到最大生物效應。
臨床意義：改變受體數量可改變細胞對 agonist 的敏感度。例如使用不可逆拮抗劑移除部分受體後，需要更高濃度的 agonist 才能達到原有最大效應。
競爭性拮抗劑與不可逆拮抗劑 競爭性拮抗劑 競爭性拮抗劑與 agonist 競爭結合同一受體位置：
特性 說明 效應可逆性 高濃度 agonist 可逆轉其效應 曲線特徵 S 形曲線向右平行移動，最大效應不變 Schild 方程式 C’/C = 1 + [I]/K_i Propranolol 是經典的競爭性 β 受體拮抗劑。
不可逆拮抗劑 不可逆拮抗劑以共價鍵與受體形成穩定鍵結：
佔據部分受體後，即使高濃度 agonist 也無法達到原有最大效應 若有備用受體存在，可維持最大效應但需要更高 agonist 濃度 Phenoxybenzamine 是 α 受體不可逆拮抗劑的代表藥物 部分激動劑（Partial Agonists） 部分激動劑佔據全部受體時仍無法產生最大效應：
特性 說明 內在活性低 只能 stabilizes 部分受體於活化構象 雙重行為 無完全 agonist 存在時表現 agonist 活性；有完全 agonist 存在時表現拮抗作用 臨床應用 Buprenorphine（μ-opioid 受體部分 agonist）比 Morphine 更安全，過量時呼吸抑制較輕 其他拮抗機制 化學性拮抗 Protamine 帶正電，臨床上用於中和帶負電的 Heparin。
生理性拮抗 不同受體系統間的對抗，例如 Insulin 對抗 Glucocorticoid hormones 的升血糖作用。
藥物動力學與藥效學的整合 時間歷程 過程 說明 分布相（α相） 藥物由血液分布到組織 消除相（β相） 藥物濃度在血液與組織間達平衡後的下降 終末半衰期 反映藥物從最深部組織清除的速率 臨床應用原則 藥物效應持續時間取決於：受體佔據時間、耦合分子的存在時間、受體脫敏機制 藥物從身體消除後，效應可能仍持續（因預存訊號分子的持續作用）

content:
Introduction 章節導讀 藥理學是研究藥物與生物體交互作用的科學，本章建立核心概念框架，包括藥效學（藥物對身體的作用）與藥物動力學（身體對藥物的處理）的基本原則，以及遺傳變異對藥物反應的深遠影響。
藥物與受體 受體的基本概念 受體（Receptor）是細胞上的特定蛋白質結構，能與藥物分子結合並引發一系列生化反應，最終導致觀察到的藥理效應。藥物作為激動劑（Agonist）激活受體，或作為拮抗劑（Antagonist）阻止受體被激活。
藥物的分子特性決定其與受體的結合能力：
藥物特性 說明 分子大小 多數藥物分子量介於 100-1000 之間 形狀與立體化學 必須與受體互補，手性（Chirality）決定對映異構物的活性差異 鍵結方式 共價鍵（強、不可逆）> 靜電鍵 > 氫鍵 > 疏水性交互作用 重要原則：鍵結越弱的藥物通常選擇性越高，因為弱鍵需要藥物與受體精確契合。
藥物-受體鍵結類型 共價鍵：強且通常不可逆，例如 Aspirin 與 cyclooxygenase 的鍵結 靜電鍵：從強離子鍵到弱氫鍵、范德華力 疏水性鍵：對脂溶性藥物與細胞膜磷脂的交互作用很重要 藥物-身體交互作用 藥效學（Pharmacodynamics） 藥物作用於身體的基本模式：
藥 物 + 受 體 → 藥 物 - 受 體 複 合 物 → 效 應 分 子 → 生 理 效 應 藥物-受體交互作用類型：
類型 說明 完全激動劑（Full Agonist） 佔據受體後產生最大效應 部分激動劑（Partial Agonist） 佔據全部受體仍無法產生最大效應；同時具有 agonist 與 antagonist 特性 競爭性拮抗劑 與 agonist 競爭結合受體，高濃度 agonist 可逆轉 不可逆拮抗劑 以共價鍵結合受體，降低最大效應且不被 agonist 逆轉 反向激動劑（Inverse Agonist） 穩定受體於非活性構象，減少基礎活性 藥物動力學（Pharmacokinetics） 身體對藥物的處理過程：
吸收（Absorption）：藥物由給藥部位進入血液 分布（Distribution）：藥物進入體內各組織區室 代謝（Metabolism）：藥物被肝臟等組織轉化 排泄（Excretion）：藥物或其代謝物離開體內 藥物穿透細胞膜 藥物穿透細胞膜的主要機制：
機制 說明 水相擴散 分子通過水溶性通道，服從 Fick’s law 脂質擴散 多數藥物的主要穿透方式；取決於藥物的 脂溶性/水溶性分配係數 特殊載體轉運 ABC 家族轉運蛋白（如 P-glycoprotein/MDR1）、SLC 家族 胞吞/胞泌 大分子藥物的摄取方式，如維生素 B₁₂ 與鐵的轉運 Henderson-Hasselbalch 方程式 弱酸與弱鹼藥物的離子化程度受 pH 影響：
酸性藥物：pH = pKa + log([A⁻]/[HA]) — 低 pH 環境中更具脂溶性 鹼性藥物：pH = pKa + log([B]/[BH⁺]) — 高 pH 環境中更具脂溶性 藥物基因體學 基因剔除與敲入技術 Knockout mice（基因剔除小鼠）：剔除特定基因，完全或部分抑制該基因功能 Knockin mice（基因敲入小鼠）：過量表現特定蛋白質 Knockdown mice：部分抑制基因表現 這些動物模型幫助研究受體或內源性配體的生理角色。
藥物基因體學（Pharmacogenomics） 研究基因變異如何影響個體間的藥物反應差異：
基因變異 臨床影響 CYP2D6 多型性 快/慢代謝者，影響 Codeine（需 CYP2D6 轉化為 morphine）、Beta-blockers 療效 CYP2C9 多型性 Warfarin 劑量需求差異 CYP2C19 多型性 影響 Clopidogrel 活化 藥物命名與法規 受體命名 採用 IUPHAR（國際藥理學聯合會）的命名標準，不同受體類型包括：
離子通道型受體（如 nAChR、GABA_A 受體） G 蛋白偶聯受體（GPCR） 酪氨酸激酶型受體（如胰島素受體） 製藥產業 真正的新藥發現需要找到新的藥物標靶（Drug Target） 藥物開發過程漫長且昂貴（平均 10-15 年，數十億美元） Big Pharma 在藥物優化、開發和商業化中扮演關鍵角色
summary:
Introduction

章節導讀

藥理學是研究藥物與生物體交互作用的科學，本章建立核心概念框架，包括藥效學（藥物對身體的作用）與藥物動力學（身體對藥物的處理）的基本原則，以及遺傳變異對藥物反應的深遠影響。

藥物與受體

受體的基本概念

受體（Receptor）是細胞上的特定蛋白質結構，能與藥物分子結合並引發一系列生化反應，最終導致觀察到的藥理效應。藥物作為激動劑（Agonist）激活受體，或作為拮抗劑（Antagonist）阻止受體被激活。

藥物的分子特性決定其與受體的結合能力：

藥物特性 說明
分子大小 多數藥物分子量介於 100-1000 之間
形狀與立體化學 必須與受體互補，手性（Chirality）決定對映異構物的活性差異
鍵結方式 共價鍵（強、不可逆）> 靜電鍵 > 氫鍵 > 疏水性交互作用

重要原則：鍵結越弱的藥物通常選擇性越高，因為弱鍵需要藥物與受體精確契合。

Introduction to Autonomic Pharmacology 章節導讀 自律神經系統調控心臟、血管、平滑肌、腺體等重要器官，本章建立自律神經藥理的基礎框架，涵蓋交感/副交感神經系統的解剖學基礎、神經傳導物質（ACh、NE）的合成與釋放，以及主要受體類型的特性。
自律神經系統的解剖學 兩大系統的對比 特性 交感神經 副交感神經 起源位置 胸腰髓（T1-L2） 腦幹/骶髓（CN III, VII, IX, X, S2-S4） 節後纖維長度 短（神經節接近椎旁） 長（神經節在效應器附近） 主要功能 「戰鬥或逃跑」 「休息與消化」 神經傳導物質 Norepinephrine（NE） Acetylcholine（ACh） 雙重神經支配（Dual Innervation） 多數器官同時接受交感與副交感神經支配，兩者通常產生相反的生理作用。
神經傳導物質化學 Acetylcholine（ACh） 項目 說明 合成 膽鹼 + Acetyl-CoA → ACh（由 ChAT 催化） 儲存 儲存於突觸囊泡 釋放 Ca²⁺依賴性胞泌 終止 Acetylcholinesterase（AChE）快速水解（數毫秒內） ACh 是以下部位的神經傳導物質：
交感和副交感節前纖維 副交感節後纖維 支配汗腺的交感纖維 骨骼肌神經肌肉接合處 Norepinephrine（NE） NE 是多數交感神經節後纖維的主要神經傳導物質。
合成途徑：酪氨酸 → L-DOPA → 多巴胺 → Norepinephrine → Epinephrine
終止方式：
攝取 1（Uptake 1）：神經末梢再攝取（主要方式） 攝取 2（Uptake 2）：周邊組織攝取 MAO 與 COMT 代謝 膽鹼性受體（Cholinoceptors） Muscarinic 受體（M1-M5） 受體 訊號機制 主要位置 M1 G_q → PLC → IP₃/DAG CNS、神經節 M2 G_i → ↓cAMP 心臟（SA/AV node） M3 G_q → PLC → IP₃/DAG 平滑肌、腺體、血管內皮 M4 G_i → ↓cAMP CNS M5 G_q → PLC → IP₃/DAG CNS Nicotinic 受體（N） 受體 說明 N_N1（神經節型） 自主神經節 N_N2（肌肉型） 神經肌肉接合處 腎上腺素性受體（Adrenoceptors） α 受體 受體 訊號機制 主要位置與功能 α1 G_q → PLC → IP₃/DAG/Ca²⁺ 血管平滑肌（收縮）、泌尿生殖道平滑肌、肝臟 α2 G_i → ↓cAMP 突觸前終末（自體受體，抑制 NE 釋放）、血小板、脂肪細胞 β 受體 受體 訊號機制 主要位置與功能 β1 G_s → ↑cAMP 心臟（正性變時/變力）、腎臟（腎素釋放） β2 G_s → ↑cAMP 支氣管平滑肌（擴張）、血管平滑肌（擴張）、骨骼肌血管 β3 G_s → ↑cAMP 脂肪細胞（脂肪分解） 自律神經系統的生理效應 目標組織 交感效應 受體 副交感效應 受體 心臟 SA node 心搏過速 β1 心搏過緩 M2 心房收縮力 增加 β1 減少 M2 AV node 傳導加快 β1 傳導減慢 M2 心室 增加收縮力 β1 — — 血管（皮膚/內臟） 收縮 α1 — — 血管（骨骼肌） 擴張(β2)/收縮(α1) α1, β2 — — 靜脈 收縮 α1, α2 — — 支氣管 擴張 β2 收縮 M3 GI 蠕動 減少 α2, β2 增加 M3 括約肌 增加張力 α1 減少張力 M3 膀胱逼尿肌 放鬆 β2 收縮 M3 膀胱括約肌 收縮 α1 放鬆 M3 瞳孔 散瞳（擴張） α1 縮瞳 M3 睫狀肌 放鬆（遠視） β 收縮（近視） M3 汗腺 分泌增加 M（交感） — — 自律神經藥物的分類 類別 作用 膽鹼激動劑 直接（M agonists）或間接（AChE 抑制劑）激活膽鹼受體 抗膽鹼藥物 競爭性阻斷 muscarinic 或 nicotinic 受體 擬交感神經藥物 直接（α/β agonists）或間接（促進 NE 釋放）激活腎上腺素受體 交感神經阻斷劑 α 或 β 受體拮抗劑 案例：Promethazine 引起的姿態性低血壓 Promethazine（phenothiazine 類抗組織胺）具有抗膽鹼和抗腎上腺素作用，抑制代償性血管收縮，故站立時血壓下降。
血壓下降刺激壓力受體反射，導致代償性心搏過速
臨床應用重點 臨床情況 代表藥物 支氣管痙攣 Albuterol（β2 agonist） 心搏過緩 Atropine（muscarinic antagonist） 高血壓 Prazosin（α1 blocker）、Propranolol（β blocker） 過敏性反應 Epinephrine（α, β agonist）

Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics 章節導讀 藥物動力學與藥效學的整合是精準給藥的基礎，本章介紹分布體積、清除率、半衰期等核心 PK 參數，以及一級動力學與容量限制動力學的臨床意義。
基本藥物動力學參數 分布體積（Volume of Distribution, V_d） 分布體積連結體內藥物量與血液或血漿中的藥物濃度：
體 內 藥 物 量 = V _ d × C （ 血 漿 濃 度 ） 特性 說明 表觀體積 V_d 可超過實際身體容積（藥物在組織中蓄積） 臨床意義 Digoxin V_d ≈ 500 L/70kg（實際體積約 70L） 清除率（Clearance, CL） 清除率是衡量身體消除藥物能力的參數：
清 除 率 = 消 除 速 率 / C （ 藥 物 濃 度 ） 總清除率 = 腎清除率 + 肝清除率 + 其他器官清除率
半衰期（Half-life, t_1/2） t_1/2 = 0.693 × V_d / CL
半衰期是劑量調整的關鍵參數，受 V_d 與 CL 兩者影響。
藥物消除動力學 一級動力學（First-order Elimination） 特性 說明 消除比例 單位時間內消除固定比例的藥物 半衰期 恆定不變 AUC 與劑量成正比 臨床意義 絕大多數藥物在此動力學範圍內 容量限制動力學（Capacity-limited/Saturable Kinetics） 重要：少數藥物在高濃度時呈現容量限制動力學：
藥物例子 臨床意義 Phenytoin 飽和代謝，小幅增加劑量可能導致濃度大幅上升 Ethanol 高濃度時呈零級動力學 Michaelis-Menten 方程式：Rate = V_max × C / (K_m + C)
穩定態與給藥設計 穩定態（Steady State） 重複給藥時，給藥速率等於消除速率時達到穩定態：
給 藥 速 率 = C L × C _ s s 參數 臨床意義 達到穩定態時間 約 4-5 個半衰期（與劑量無關） 穩定態濃度 與給藥速率成正比，與清除率成反比 維持劑量與負荷劑量 公式 應用 維持劑量速率 = CL × C_ss / F 持續維持目標濃度 負荷劑量 = V_d × C_target 快速達到目標濃度 生物可用率（Bioavailability, F） 給藥途徑 F 值 說明 靜脈注射 100% 完全進入體循環 口服 變動 受吸收不全與首渡肝臟代謝影響 其他 各異 取決於給藥途徑的吸收特性 首渡效應（First-pass Effect）：口服藥物經肝臟首次通過時的部分代謝，導致 F < 100%。
腎功能與肝功能衰竭時的劑量調整 腎功能衰竭 Cockcroft-Gault 方程式估算肌酸酐清除率：
CrCl = [(140 - 年齡) × 體重(kg)] / [72 × 血清肌酸酐(mg/dL)]（女性 × 0.85）
藥物 腎衰竭時調整 Digoxin 腎功能不良患者需減少劑量 Aminoglycosides 顯著依賴腎清除，需监测血藥濃度 血漿蛋白結合置換 臨床意義 說明 游離藥物濃度 不改變 總藥物濃度 可能下降 臨床影響 有限（消除率不變） 重要藥物動力學數據 藥物 半衰期 (h) 分布體積 (L/70kg) 清除途徑 治療濃度範圍 Digoxin 39 500 67% 腎, 33% 肝 1 ng/mL Warfarin 37 9.8 97% 肝代謝 INR 2-3 Phenytoin 濃度依賴 45 肝代謝 10-20 mg/L Theophylline 8.1 35 肝代謝 10-20 mg/L Lithium 22 55 95% 腎 0.7-1.2 mEq/L Gentamicin 3 20 76% 腎 3 mg/L (peak) Lidocaine 1.8 77 肝血流依賴 3-6 mg/L 窄治療指數藥物：Digoxin、Lithium、Theophylline、Gentamicin — 需監測血藥濃度

Vasodilators and Treatment of Angina Pectoris 章節導讀 血管擴張劑與心絞痛治療是心血管藥理的核心應用。本章涵蓋硝酸鹽類、鈣離子通道阻斷劑、ACE 抑制劑、ARB 等藥物在高血壓與心絞痛中的臨床應用。

章節導讀

血管擴張劑與心絞痛治療是心血管藥理的核心應用。本章涵蓋硝酸鹽類、鈣離子通道阻斷劑、ACE 抑制劑、ARB 等藥物在高血壓與心絞痛中的臨床應用。

中樞性交感神經抑制劑

Clonidine

特性 說明
機轉 中樞性 α2 激動劑，減少交感神經輸出
副作用 鎮靜、口乾
停藥反彈 高劑量長期使用後突然停藥可致高血壓危象

Methyldopa

特性 說明
機轉 中樞性 α2 激動劑（偽神經傳導物質）
臨床特點 懷孕時高血壓的首選藥物之一
副作用 鎮靜、肝功能異常、Coombs 試驗陽性

腎上腺素神經阻斷劑

Guanethidine

特性 說明
機轉 阻斷 NE 從交感神經末梢釋放（攝取進入囊泡置換 NE）
副作用 姿勢性低血壓、腹瀉、性功能障礙
現況 臨床上已少用

Reserpine

特性 說明
機轉 阻斷囊泡攝取和儲存單胺類神經傳導物質
副作用 憂鬱、精神病（中樞胺類耗竭）、帕金森氏症症狀、胃腸道不適

直接血管擴張劑

Hydralazine

特性 說明
機轉 釋放 NO，擴張小動脈（對靜脈作用小）
臨床用途 高血壓；與硝酸鹽合用治療心衰竭
副作用 反射性心搏過速、紅斑性狼瘡樣症候群（劑量 > 400 mg/day）

Minoxidil

特性 說明
機轉 開啟 K⁺ 通道，穩定平滑肌細胞膜
臨床用途 嚴重或腎衰竭相關高血壓
副作用 反射性心搏過速、多毛症（女性困擾）

Sodium Nitroprusside

特性 說明
機轉 釋放 NO，激活 guanylyl cyclase → ↑cGMP
作用時間 數分鐘內生效，停藥後效應立即消失
臨床用途 高血壓急症
副作用 氰化物中毒（嚴重）

Diazoxide

特性 說明
機轉 開啟 K⁺ 通道
臨床用途 高血壓急症
副作用 過度低血壓、高血糖

Fenoldopam

特性 說明
機轉 Dopamine D1 受體激動劑
臨床用途 高血壓急症、術後高血壓

ACE 抑制劑

作用機制

ACE 抑制劑抑制血管張力素轉化酶，減少血管張力素 II 生成並增加 bradykinin 作用。

章節導讀 本章節說明 β-內醯胺抗生素（Penicillins、Cephalosporins、Carbapenems）與其他細胞壁活性抗生素（Vancomycin、Daptomycin）的作用機轉、抗菌譜與臨床應用。
Beta-Lactam & Cell Wall-Active Antibiotics 作用機轉 β-內醯胺抗生素藉由抑制細菌細胞壁的轉肽酶（transpeptidase）反應來阻止肽聚糖（peptidoglycan）合成。當細胞壁無法形成時，細菌因滲透壓差而溶解死亡。
β-lactamases（β-內醯胺酶）可水解 β-lactam 環，使抗生素失效。這是細菌產生抗藥性的主要機制之一。
青黴素類（Penicillins） 分類：
標準青黴素（如 penicillin G）：對革蘭氏陽性菌、革蘭氏陰性球菌有效，但易被 β-lactamases 水解 抗葡萄球菌青黴素（如 nafcillin、oxacillin、dicloxacillin）：對 MRSA 有效 廣效青黴素（如 amoxicillin、ampicillin、piperacillin）：對革蘭氏陰性桿菌有較好活性 常見藥物：
penicillin G：注射製劑，用於梅毒、肺炎球菌腦膜炎 amoxicillin：口服製劑，用於呼吸道、泌尿道感染 piperacillin：廣效，對綠膿桿菌（P aeruginosa）有效 頭孢菌素類（Cephalosporins） 頭孢菌素依抗菌譜分為五代：
世代 藥物 特色 第一代 cephalexin、cefazolin 革蘭氏陽性为主 第二代 cefuroxime 對 H influenzae、M catarrhalis 有效 第三代 ceftriaxone、cefotaxime 腦膜炎、肺炎、淋病 第四代 cefepime 對 綠膿桿菌有效 第五代 ceftaroline 對 MRSA 有效 碳青黴烯類（Carbapenems） imipenem、meropenem、ertapenem 為超廣效抗生素，對革蘭氏陽性菌、革蘭氏陰性菌、厭氧菌均有效。對大多數 β-lactamases 穩定。
單環類（Monobactams） aztreonam 僅對革蘭氏陰性菌（尤其是綠膿桿菌）有效，對革蘭氏陽性菌和厭氧菌無效。適用於對青黴素過敏的患者。
糖肽類（Glycopeptides） vancomycin：對MRSA、表皮葡萄球菌、腸球菌有效。為最後一線藥物（last resort drug）。主要副作用為腎毒性和耳毒性。
teicoplanin：類似 vancomycin，但半衰期較長，可靜脈或肌肉注射。
酯類（Daptomycin） daptomycin 為 lipopeptide 抗生素，作用於細菌細胞膜，使細胞膜去極化。對MRSA、vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus（VRE）有效。不用於肺炎（會被肺表面活性劑抑制）。
抗藥性機制 β-lactamases 水解：最常見的抗藥性機制 PBP 改變：如 MRSA 的 mecA 基因產生低親和性 PBP 藥物滲透障礙：革蘭氏陰性菌外膜 porin 通道改變 外排泵（Efflux pump）：將藥物排出菌體 臨床應用要點 Penicillin 過敏者若僅有皮疹，可考慮使用 cephalosporins（交叉過敏反應 < 1-2%） Penicillin 過敏者若有全身性過敏反應（anaphylaxis），應避免所有 β-lactams ceftriaxone 可用於細菌性腦膜炎的初始治療 vancomycin 需監測血中濃度（trough level 10-15 mcg/mL 用於 MRSA 肺炎） 重點摘要 β-內醯胺抗生素抑制細胞壁合成，具 bactericidal作用 青黴素類分為三群：標準、抗葡萄球菌、广效 頭孢菌素類分為五代，各有抗菌譜特點 Vancomycin 為對抗 MRSA、Enterococcus 的最後一線藥物 β-lactamase 抑制劑（如 clavulanate、tazobactam）可保護 β-lactam 抗生素不被水解 藥物總表 藥物名稱 分類 抗菌譜 主要副作用 penicillin G 青黴素 革蘭氏陽性、螺旋體 過敏反應 amoxicillin 廣效青黴素 呼吸道、泌尿道 腹瀉、過敏 nafcillin 抗葡萄球菌 MRSA 肝毒性 piperacillin 廣效+抗綠膿 綠膿桿菌、克雷白氏菌 出血傾向 cefazolin 第一代頭孢 手術預防 腎毒性 ceftriaxone 第三代頭孢 腦膜炎、肺炎、淋病 膽汁淤積 cefepime 第四代頭孢 綠膿桿菌、肺炎 腦病變 imipenem 碳青黴烯 超廣效 癲癇（高劑量） vancomycin 糖肽類 MRSA、腸球菌 腎毒性、耳毒性 daptomycin 酯類 MRSA、VRE 肌痛（不用於肺炎）

TRH（甲狀腺刺激素釋放激素）、CRH（皮促素釋放激素） GnRH（性腺刺激素釋放激素）、GHRH（生長激素釋放激素） Somatostatin（體抑素）：抑制 GH、TSH 等多種激素 下視丘通過腦下垂體門脈系統調控腦下垂體前葉 腦下垂體前葉激素

Introduction 660 SECTION VII Endocrine Drugs Drugs that mimic or block the effects of <span style=“colopituitary">hypothalamic and pituitary hormones have pharmacologic applications in three primary areas: (1) as replacement therapy for hormone deficiency spituitary) as antagonists for diseases caused by excess production of pituitary hormones; and (3) as diagnostic tools for identifying several endocrine abnormalities.
HYPOTHALAMIC REGULATORS All the hormones produced by the anterior pituitary except pro- lactin (PRL) are key participants in hormonal systems in which they regulate the production of hormones and autocrine-paracrine factors by endocrine glands and other peripheral tissues. In tpituitaryems, the sechypothalamice pituitary hormone is under the con- trol of one or more hypothalamic hormones. Each hypothalamic- pituitary-endocrine gland system or axis provides multiple opportunities for complex neuroendocrine regulation of growth and development, metabolism, and reproductive function.
HYPOTHALAMIC HORMONE RECEPTORS The anterior pituitary hormones can be classified according to hormone structure and the types of receptors that they activate. <span style=“colGH:#60a5fa”>Growth hormone (GH) and prolactin , single-chain protein hormones with significant homology, form one group. Both hormones activate receptors of the JAK/STAT superfamily (see Chapter 2 ). Three pituitary hormones— thyroid-stimulating hormone (<spanthyrotropinor:#60a5fa”>TSH, thyrotropin), fo<span style=<span style=“color:#6LH5fa”>luteinizing hormonecle-stimulating hormone (FSH) , and luteinizing hormone (LH) —are dimeric TSHteins that activate G protein-coupled receptors (see Chapter 2 ). TSH, FSH, and LH share a common α chain. Their β chains, though somewhat similar to each other, differ enough to confer receptor A C R O N Y M S <spanAcorticotropinropic hormone AdrenocorticoCorticotropine (corticotropin)<spGrowth hormoner:#60a5fa">GHRH Corticotropin-releasing hormone FSH Follicle-stimulating hormone GH Growth hormone GHRH Growth hormone-releasing hormone <spanGonadotropin-releasing hormonepan> Gonadotropin-releasing hormone hCG Human chorionic gonadotropin hMG Human menopausal gonadotropin IGF Insulin-like growtThyr<spaProlactincolor:#60a5fa">PRLopin Luteinizing hormone PRL Prolactin rhGH Recombinant human growth hormone SST Somatostatin TRH Thyrotropin-releasing hormone TSH Thyroid-stimulating hormone (thyrotropin) DA Posterior pituitary Endocrine glands, liver, bone PRLther tissues Target tissues Portal venous system GnRHrior pituitary + – Hypothalamus SST Oxytocin ADH PRL GHRH TRH CRH GnRH GH TSH ACTH LH FSH FIGURE 37–1 The hypothalamic-pituitary endocrine system. Except for prolactin, hormones released from the anterior pituitary stimulate the production of hormones by a peripheral endocrine gland, the liver, or other tissues. Prolactin and the hormones released from the posterior pituitary (vasopressin and oxytocin) act directly on target tissues. Hypothalamic factors regulate the release of ante- rior pituitary hormones. ACTH, adrenocorticotropin; ADH, antidi- uretic hormone [vasopressin]; CRH, corticotropin-releasing hormone; DA, doGnRHne; FSH, follicle-stimulating hormone; GH, growth hor- mone; GHRH, growth hormone-releasing hormone; GnRH, gonado- tropin-releasing hormone; LH, luteinizing hormone; PRL, prolactin; SST, somatostatin; TRH, thyrotropin-releasing hormone; TSH, thyroid- stimulating hormone.
CHAPTER 37 Hypothalamic & Pituitary Hormones 661 specificity. Finally, adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) , a single peptide cleaved from a larger precursor that also contains the peptide β-endorphin (see Chapter 31 ), represents a third cat- egory. Like TSH, LH, and FSH, ACTH acts through a G protein- coupled receptor. A unique feature of the ACTH receptor (also known as the melanocortin 2 receptor) is that a transmembrane protein, melanocortin 2 receptor accessory protein, is essential for normal ACTH receptor trafficking and signaling. TSH, FSH, LH, and ACTH share similarities in the regulation of their release from the pituitary. Each is under the control of a distinctive hypothalamic peptide that stimulates their production by acting on G protein-coupled receptors ( Table 37–1 ). TSH release is regulated by thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH) , whereas the release of LH and FSH (known collectively as gonad- otropins) is stimulated by pulses of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH). ACTH release is stimulated by corticotro- pin-releasing hormone (CRH). An important regulatory feature shared by these four structurally related hormones is that they and their hypothalamic releasing factors are subject to feedback inhib- itory regulation by the hormones whose production they control. TSH and TRH production are inhibited by the two key thyroid hormones, thyroxine and triiodothyronine (see Chapter 38 ). Gonadotropin and GnRH production is inhibited in women by estrogen and progesterone, and in men by testosterone and other androgens. ACTH and CRH production are inhibited by cortisol. Feedback regulation is critical to the physiologic control of thy- roid, adrenal cortical, and gonadal function and is also important in pharmacologic treatments that affect these systems. The hypothalamic hormonal control of GH and prolactin differs from the regulatory systems for TSH, FSH, LH, and ACTH. The hypothalamus secretes two hormones that regulate GH; growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) stimulates GH production, whereas the peptide somatostatin (SST) inhibits GH production. GH and its primary peripheral mediator, insu- lin-like growth factor-I (IGF-I) , also provide feedback to inhibit GH release. Prolactin production is inhibited by the catecholamine dopamine acting through the D 2 subtype of dopamine receptors. The hypothalamus does not produce a hormone that specifically stimulates prolactin secretion, although TRH can stimulate prolactin release, particularly when TRH concentrations are high in the setting of primary hypothyroidism. Whereas all the pituitary and hypothalamic hormones described previously are available for use in humans, only a few are of major clinical importance. Because of the greater ease of administration of target endocrine gland hormones or their synthetic analogs, the related hypothalamic and pituitary hormones (TRH, TSH, CRH, ACTH, GHRH) are used infrequently as treatments. Some, such as ACTH, are used for specialized diagnostic testing. These agents are described in Tables 37–2 and 37–3 and are not discussed fur- ther in this chapter. In contrast, GH, SST, LH, FSH, GnRH, and dopamine or analogs of these hormones are commonly used and are described in the following text.
TABLE 37–1 Links between hypothalamic, anterior pituitary, and target organ hormone or mediator.1
Anterior Pituitary Hormone Hypothalamic Hormone Target Organ Primary Target Organ Hormone or Mediator Growth hormone (GH, somatotropin) Growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) (+) Somatostatin (−) Liver, bone, muscle, kidney, and others Insulin-like growth factor-I (IGF-I) Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) GROWTH HORMONE (SOMATOTROPIN) Growth hormone, an anterior pituitary hormone, is required dur- ing childhood and adolescence for attainment of normal adult size and has important effects throughout postnatal life on lipid and carbohydrate metabolism, and on lean body mass and bone den- sity. Its growth-promoting effects are primarily mediated via IGF-I ( also known as somatomedin C). Individuals with coGHenital or acquired deficiency of GH during childhood or adolescence fail to reach their predicted adult height and have dispropGHtionately increased body fat and decreased muscle mass. Adults with Growth hormonealso have disproportionately low lean body mass. Chemistry & Pharmacokinetics A. Structure Growth hormone is a 191-amino-acid peptide with two sulfhydryl bridges. Its structure closely resembles that of prolactin. In the past, medicinal GH was isolated from the pituitaries of human cadavers. However, this form of GH was found to be contami- nated with prions that could cause Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. For this reason, it is no longer used. Somatropin , the recombinant form of GH, has a 191-amino-acid sequence that is identical with the predominant native form of human GH. B. Absorption, Metabolism, and Excretion Circulating endogenous GH has a half-life of 20–25 minutes and is predominantly cleared by the liver. Recombinant human GH (rhGH) is administered subcutaneously 6–7 times per week. Peak levels occur in 2–4 hours and active blood levels persist for approximately 36 hours. Pharmacodynamics Growth hormone mediates its effects via cell surface receptors of the JAK/STAT cytokine receptor superfamily. Growth hormone has two distinct GH receptor binding sites. Dimerization of two GH receptors is stimulated by a single GH molecule and acti- vates signaling cascades mediated by receptor-associated JAK tyrosine kinases and STATs (see Chapter 2 ). GH has complex effects on growth, body composition, and carbohydrate, protein, and lipid metabolism. The growth-promoting effects are medi- ated principally througIGFIGFpan>n increase in the produIGFon of IGF-I. Much of the circulating IGF-I is produced in the liver. GH also stimulates production of IGF-I in bone, cartilage, muscle, kid- ney, and other tissues, where it plays autocrine or paracrine roles. GH stimulates longitudinal bone growth until the epiphyses close—near the end of puberty. In both children and adults, GH has anabolic effects in muscle and catabolic effects in lipid cells that shift the balance of body mass to an increase in muscle mass and a reduction in adiposity. The direct and indirect effects of GH on carbohydrate metabolism are mixed, in part because GH and IGF-I have opposite effects on insulin sensitivity. GH reduces insulin sensitivity, which results in mild hyperinsulin- emia, whereas IGF-I has insulin-like effects on glucose transport. In patients who are unable to respond to GH because of severe GH resistance (caused by GH receptor mutations, post-GH receptor signaling mutations, or GH antibodies), the administra- tion of recombinant human IGF-I may cause hypoglycemia because of its insulin-like effects. Clinical Pharmacology A. Growth Hormone Deficiency GH deficiency can have a genetic basis, may be associated with midline developmental defect syndromes (eg, septo-optic dysplasia), or can be acq<span style="hypothalamuse">pituitarya result of damage to the pituitary or hypothalamus by a trauma (including breech or traumatic delivery), intracranial tumors, infection, infiltrative or hemorrhagic pro- cesses, or irradiation. Neonates with isolated GH deficiency are typically of normal size at birth because prenatal growth is not GH-dependent. In contrast, IGF-I is essential for normal prenatal and postnatal growth. Through poorly understood mechanisms, IGF-I expression and postnatal growth become GH-dependent during the first year of life. In childhood, GH deficiency typically presents as short stature, often with mild adiposity. Another early sign of GH deficiency is hypoglycemia due to unopposed action of insulin, to which young children are especially sensitive. Criteria for diagnosis of GH deficiency usually include (1) a subnormal height velocity for age and (2) a subnormal serum GH response following stimulation with at least two GH secretagogues. The prevalence of GH deficiency is approximately 1:5000. Therapy with rhGH permits many children with short stature due to GH deficiency to achieve normal adult height. In the past, it was believed that adults with GH deficiency do not exhibit a significant syndrome. However, more detailed studies suggest that adults with GH deficiency often have gener- alized obesity, reduced muscle mass, asthenia, and reduced car- diac output. GH-deficient adults who have been treated with GH have been shown to experience a reversal of many of these manifestations. B. Growth Hormone Treatment of Pediatric Patients with Short Stature Although the greatest improvement in growth occurs in patients with GH deficiency, exogenous GH has some effect on height in
TABLE 37–3 Diagnostic uses of thyroid-stimulating
hormone and adrenocorticotropin. Hormone Diagnostic Use Thyroid-stimulating hormone (<spanthyrotropinor:#60a5fa">TSH; thyrotropin) In patients who have been treated TSHgically for thyroid carcinoma, to test for recurrence by assessing TSH-stimulated whole-body 131I scans and serum thyroglobulin determinations Adrenocorticotropin (ACTH) CHAPTER 37 Hypothalamic & Pituitary Hormones 663 children with short stature caused by factors other than GH defi- ciency. GH has been approved for several conditions ( Table 37–4 ) and has been used experimentally or off-label in many others. Prader-Willi syndrome is an autosomal dominant genetic disease associated with growth failure, obesity, and carbohydrate intoler- ance. In children with Prader-Willi syndrome and growth failure, GH treatment decreases body fat and increases lean body mass, linear growth, and energy expenditure. GH treatment has also been shown to have a strong beneficial effect on final height of girls with Turner syndrome (45 X karyo- type and variants). In clinical trials, GH treatment has been shown to increase final height in girls with Turner syndrome by 10–15 cm (4–6 inches). Because girls with Turner syndrome also have either absent or rudimentary ovaries, GH must be judiciously combined with gonadal steroids to achieve maximal height. Other condi- tions of pediatric growth failure for which GH treatment is FDA- approved include chronic renal insufficiency pre-transplant and small-for-gestational-age at birth in which the child’s height remains more than 2 standard deviations below the norm at 2 years of age. A controversial but approved use of GH is for children with idiopathic short stature (ISS). This is a heterogeneous popula- tion that has in common no identifiable cause of the short stature. Some have arbitrarily defined ISS clinically as having a height at least 2.25 standard deviations below the norm for children of the same age and an unlikelihood of achieving an adult height that will be less than 2.25 standard deviations below the norm. In this group of children, many years of GH therapy result in an average increase in adult height of 4–7 cm (1.57–2.76 inches) at a cost of $5000–$40,000 per year. The complex issues involved in the cost- risk-benefit relationship of this use of GH are important because an estimated 400,000 children in the United States fit the diag- nostic criteria for ISS. Treatment of children with short stature should be carried out by specialists experienced in GH administration. GH dose require- ments vary with the condition being treated, with GH-deficient children typically being most responsive. Children must be observed closely for slowing of growth velocity, which could indicate a need to increase the dosage or the possibility of epiphyseal fusion or intercurrent problems such as hypothyroidism or malnutrition. Other Uses of Growth Hormone Growth hormone affects many organ systems and also has a net anabolic effect. It has been tested in a number of conditions that are associated with a severe catabolic state and is approved for the treatment of wasting in patients with AIDS. In 2004, GH was approved for treatment of patients with short bowel syndrome who are dependent on total parenteral nutrition (TPN). After intestinal resection or bypass, the remaining functional intestine in many patients undergoes extensive adaptation that allows it to adequately absorb nutrients. However, other patients fail to ade- quately adapt and develop a malabsorption syndrome. GH has been shown to increase intestinal growth and improve its function in experimental animals. Benefits of GH treatment for patients with short bowel syndrome and dependence on total parenteral nutrition have mostly been short-lived in the clinical studies that have been published to date. Growth hormone is administered with glutamine, which also has trophic effects on the intestinal mucosa. GH is a popular component of “anti-aging” programs. Serum levels of GH normally decline with aging; anti-aging programs claim that injection of GH or administration of drugs purported to increase GH release are effective anti-aging remedies. These claims are largely unsubstantiated. In contrast studies in mice and the nematode C elegans have clearly demonstrated that ana- logs of human GH and IGF-I consistently shorten life span and that loss-of-function mutations in the signaling pathways for the GH and IGF-I analogs lengthen life span. Another use of GH is by athletes for a purported increase in muscle mass and athletic performance. GH is one of the drugs banned by the Olympic Committee. Although GH has important effects on lipid and carbohydrate metabolism and on lean body mass, it does not seem likely to be a fruitful direct target for efforts to develop new drugs to treat obe- sity. However, some of the hormonal and neuroendocrine systems that regulate GH secretion are being investigated as possible targets for antiobesity drugs (see Box: Treatment of Obesity). In 1993, the FDA approved the use of recombinant bovine growth hormone (rbGH) in dairy cattle to increase milk produc- tion. Although milk and meat from rbGH-treated cows appear to be safe, these cows have a higher incidence of mastitis, which could increase antibiotic use and result in greater antibiotic resi- dues in milk and meat.
TABLE 37–4 Clinical uses of recombinant human
growth hormone. Primary Therapeutic Objective Clinical Condition Growth Growth failure in pediatric patients associated with: Growth hormone deficiency Chronic renal insufficiency pre-transplant Noonan syndrome Prader-Willi syndrome TREATMENT OF OBESITY 1 It is said that the developed world is experiencing an “epidemic of obesity.” This statement is based on statistics showing that in the USA, for example, 30–40% of the population is above optimal weight and that the excess weight (especially abdominal fat) is often associated with the metabolic syndrome and increased risks of cardiovascular disease and diabetes. Since eating behav- ior is an expression of endocrine, neurophysiologic, and psycho- logical processes, prevention and treatment of obesity are complex. It is not surprising that there is considerable scientific and financial interest in developing pharmacologic therapy for the condition. Although obesity can be defined as excess adipose tissue, it is currently quantitated by means of the body mass index (BMI), calculated from BMI = weight (in kilograms)/height2 (in meters). Using this measure, a normal BMI is defined as 18.5–24.9; over- weight, 25–29.9; obese, 30–39.9; and morbidly obese (ie, at very high risk), ≥ 40. Some extremely muscular individuals may have a BMI higher than 25 and no excess fat; however, the BMI scale generally correlates with the degree of obesity and with risk. Although the cause of obesity can be simply stated as energy intake (dietary calories) exceeding energy output (resting metab- olism plus exercise), the actual physiology of weight control is extremely complex, and the pathophysiology of obesity is still poorly understood. Many hormones and neuronal mechanisms regulate intake (appetite, satiety), processing (absorption, conver- sion to fat, glycogen, etc), and output (thermogenesis, muscle work). The fact that a large number of hormones reduce appetite (Table 37–4.1, see online version of this book) might appear to offer many targets for weight-reducing drug therapy, but despite intensive research, no available pharmacologic therapy has succeeded in maintaining a weight loss of over 10% for 1 year. Furthermore, the social and psychological aspects of eating are powerful influences that are independent of or only partially dependent on the physiologic control mechanisms. In contrast, bariatric (weight-reducing) surgery readily achieves a sustained weight loss of 10–40%. Furthermore, surgery that bypasses the stomach and upper small intestine (but not simple restrictive banding) rapidly reverses some aspects of the metabolic syndrome even before significant weight is lost. However, even a 5–10% loss of weight is associated with a reduction in blood pres- sure and improved glycemic control. Until approximately 15 years ago, the most popular and successful appetite suppressants were the nonselective 5-HT 2 agonists: fenfluramine and dexfenfluramine. Combined with phentermine as Fen-Phen and Dex-Phen, they were moderately effective. However, these drugs were found to cause pulmonary hypertension and cardiac valve defects and were withdrawn. Older drugs still available in the United States and some other countries include phenylpropanolamine, benzphetamine, amphet- amine, methamphetamine, phentermine, diethylpropion, mazindol, and phendimetrazine. These drugs are all amphetamine mimics and are central nervous system appetite suppressants; they are generally helpful only during the first few weeks of therapy. Their toxicity is significant and includes hypertension (with a risk of cerebral hemor- rhage) and addiction liability. Orlistat is the only non-amphetamine drug currently approved in the United States for the treatment of obesity. Two other drugs that have been intensely studied are listed in Table 37–5. Clinical trials and phase 4 reports suggest that orlistat is modestly effec- tive for the duration of therapy (up to 1 year) and is probably safer than the amphetamine mimics. However, it does not pro- duce more than a 5–10% loss of weight. Sibutramine was mar- keted for several years but was withdrawn because of increasing evidence of cardiovascular toxicity. Lorcaserin received intense study through 2010 and was submitted for approval to the FDA, but this was denied on the basis of considerations of inadequate safety and effectiveness. Because of the low efficacy of the drugs listed in Table 37–5, intensive research continues. (Some drugs approved for other indications that reduce appetite and possible future weight loss drugs are set forth in Table 37–5.1, see online version of this book). Because of the redundancy of the physiologic mecha- nisms for control of body weight, it seems likely that polyphar- macy targeting multiple pathways will be needed to achieve success. 1Contributed by B.G. Katzung.

MECASERMIN A smallGHumber of children with growth failure have severe IGF-I deficiency that is not responsive to exogenous GH. Causes include mutations in the GH receptor and in the GH receptor signaling pathway, IGFtralizing antibodies to GH, and IGF-I gIGF dIGFcts. In 2005, the FDA approved two forms of recombinant human IGF-I (rhIGF-I) for treatment of severe IGF-I deficiency that is not responsive to GH: mecasermin and mecasermin rinfabate. Mecasermin is rhIGF-I alone, while mecasermin rinfabate is a complex of recombinant human IGF-I (rhIGF-I) and recombi- nant human insulin-like growth factor-binding protein-3 (rhIGFBP-3). This binding protein significantly increases the cir- culating half-life of rhIGF-I. Normally, the great majority of the circulating IGF-I is bound to IGFBP-3, which is produced prin- cipally by the liver under the control of GH. Mecasermin rinfa- bate is not currently available in the United States. Mecasermin is administered subcutaneously twice daily at a recommended start- ing dosage of 0.04–0.08 mg/kg and increased weekly up to a maximum twice-daily dosage of 0.12 mg/kg. The most important adverse effect observed with mecasermin is hypoglycemia. To avoid hypoglycemia, the prescribing instruc- tions require consumption of a carbohydrate-containing meal or snack 20 minutes before or after mecasermin administration. Several patients have experienced intracranial hypertension and asymptomatic elevation of liver enzymes.
GROWTH HORMONE ANTAGONISTS The need for antagonists of GHGHspan> stems from the tendency oGHGH-producing cells (somatotrophs) in the anteGHor pituitary</Pituitaryform GH-secreting tumors. Pituitary adenomas occur most commonly in adults. In adults, GH-secreting adenomas cause acromegaly , which is characterized by abnormal growth of cartilage and bone tissue, and many organs including skin, muscle, heart, liver, and the gastroin- testinal tract. Acromegaly adversely affects the skeletal, muscular, cardiovascular, respiratory, and metabolic systems. When a GH-secreting adenoma occurs before the long bone epiphyses close, it leads to the rare condition, gigantism . Small GH-secreting adenomas can be treated with GH antagonists. These include somatostatin analogs and dopamine receptor agonists, which reduce the production of GH, and the novel GH receptor antago- nist pegvisomanpituitary prevents GH from activating GH signal- ing pathways. Larger pituitary adenomas produce greater amounts of GH and also can impair visual and central nervous system func- tion by encroaching on nearby brain structures. The kidney appears to play an important role in its metabolism and excretion. 下視丘分泌的釋放/抑制激素

  • 下視丘通過腦下垂體門脈系統調控腦下垂體前葉

腦下垂體前葉激素

  • TSH（甲狀腺刺激素）、ACTH（皮促素）
  • FSH/LH（促性腺激素）、PRL（泌乳素）、GH（生長激素）

生長激素

  • 促進蛋白質合成、脂肪分解、胰島素阻抗
  • IGF-1（胰島素樣生長因子）介導多數生長激素作用

章節導讀 中樞神經刺激藥物涵蓋了從治療注意力不足過動症（ADHD）的精神刺激劑到用於嗜睡症與肥胖的藥物。本章節系統探討這類藥物的分類、作用機轉、臨床應用與不良反應，包括 Methylphenidate、Amphetamines、Modafinil、Caffeine等常用藥物，以及它們的濫用潛力與管理策略。
CNS Stimulants CNS stimulants encompass a range of drugs from psychostimulants used to treat attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) to agents for narcolepsy and obesity. This chapter systematically explores the classification, mechanisms of action, clinical applications, and adverse effects of these drugs, including commonly used agents such as Methylphenidate, Amphetamines, Modafinil, and Caffeine, as well as their abuse potential and management strategies.

CNS stimulants encompass a range of drugs from psychostimulants used to treat attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) to agents for narcolepsy and obesity. This chapter systematically explores the classification, mechanisms of action, clinical applications, and adverse effects of these drugs, including commonly used agents such as Methylphenidate, Amphetamines, Modafinil, and Caffeine, as well as their abuse potential and management strategies.

B - Breathing（呼吸） 評估呼吸；脈搏血氧儀；必要時機械換氣
C - Circulation（循環） 建立靜脈通路；持續監測脈搏、血壓、尿量
D - Drugs（藥物/去污染） 血糖檢測；解毒劑；清除污染

初始藥物處置

藥物 劑量 適應症

content:
CH53 免疫藥理學 章節導讀 免疫藥理學涵蓋免疫系統的藥理學調節，包括免疫抑制劑、免疫增強劑及抗發炎藥物。本章節介紹免疫系統的基本組成（先天性與適應性免疫）、免疫抑制劑（環孢素、他克莫司、黴酚酸酯、皮質類固醇等）的藥理學特性與臨床應用，以及超敏反應與自體免疫疾病的治療原則。
免疫系統概述 先天性免疫（Innate Immunity） 組成 功能 補體系統（C1-C9） 細菌裂解（膜攻擊複合體MAC）；調理作用；化學趨化作用 吞噬細胞 嗜中性球、巨噬細胞；吞噬並消化病原體 自然殺手細胞（NK cells） 殺死病毒感染細胞及腫瘤細胞 樹突細胞 抗原呈遞；連結先天性與適應性免疫 適應性免疫（Adaptive Immunity） 組成 功能 T淋巴細胞 細胞媒介免疫；CD4⁺ helper T cells（TH1/TH2/TH17）；CD8⁺ cytotoxic T cells B淋巴細胞 體液免疫；抗體產生；漿細胞與記憶B細胞 抗體（IgG, IgM, IgA, IgE, IgD） 中和毒素；調理作用；補體活化 T細胞活化所需的兩個信號 信號 描述 信號1 TCR與MHC-胜肽複合體結合 信號2（共同刺激） 抗原呈遞細胞的CD80/CD86與T細胞的CD28結合 負向調控 CTLA-4與CD80/CD86親和力更高，抑制T細胞活化 超敏反應分類 第一型（立即型）— IgE媒介 機轉：過敏原與肥大細胞/嗜鹼性球表面的IgE結合，導致去顆粒，釋出組織胺、白三烯等介質。
臨床表現 說明 全身性過敏反應 威脅生命的氣道水腫、血壓下降 氣喘 支氣管收縮、黏液分泌 過敏性鼻炎 打噴嚏、鼻塞 蕁麻疹 皮膚風疹塊、瘙癢 第二型（細胞毒型）— IgG/IgM抗體 機轉：抗體與細胞表面或細胞外基質抗原結合，透過補體活化或ADCC導致細胞損傷。
臨床範例 說明 輸血反應 血型不合導致溶血 Rh不相容 母體抗Rh抗體攻擊胎兒紅血球 藥物誘導性溶血 Penicillin等藥物結合紅血球形成新抗原 第三型（免疫複合體型） 機轉：抗原-抗體複合體沉積於血管壁或腎絲球，補體活化導致組織損傷。
臨床範例 說明 血清病 藥物或異源蛋白引起；發燒、關節炎、腎炎 局部Arthus反應 注射部位壞死 腎絲球腎炎 免疫複合體沉積 第四型（遲發型）— 細胞媒介 機轉：TH1細胞釋放IFN-γ等細胞激素，招募並活化巨噬細胞，導致組織損傷。
臨床範例 說明 結核菌素反應 結核菌素皮膚試驗 接觸性過敏 毒葛過敏（pentadecacatechol） 移植排斥反應 急性細胞媒介排斥 免疫抑制劑 鈣神經磷酸酶抑制劑（Calcineurin Inhibitors） cyclosporine（環孢素） 作用機轉：與cyclophilin結合形成複合體，抑制calcineurin，阻斷IL-2基因轉錄，抑制T細胞活化。
特性 說明 適應症 器官移植（肝、腎、心）；自體免疫疾病 給藥途徑 口服或靜脈（微乳劑型Neoral） 半衰期 約24小時（變異性大） 治療藥物監測 目標谷底濃度：移植後100-250 ng/mL（各中心略有不同） 不良反應 系統 表現 腎臟 急性腎毒性（可逆性）；慢性腎間質纖維化 高血壓 常見（calcineurin抑制導致血管收縮） 神經 顫抖、頭痛、感覺異常 齒齦增生 齒齦肥大（常見） 多毛症 臉部及全身毛髮增加 感染 機會性感染（CMV、BK病毒、JC病毒） tacrolimus（他克莫司，FK506） 作用機轉：與FK506 binding protein (FKBP-12) 結合，抑制calcineurin，與cyclosporine相似但效力更強。
特性 說明 效力 約100倍於cyclosporine 適應症 肝、腎移植；類風濕關節炎、乾癬 給藥途徑 口服（緩釋膠囊）或靜脈 治療藥物監測 目標谷底濃度：10-15 ng/mL（早期）；5-10 ng/mL（維持期） 不良反應 系統 表現 腎臟 急性腎毒性（與cyclosporine相似） 神經 手部顫抖（比cyclosporine常見）；頭痛、失眠 代謝 糖尿病（新發生糖尿病風險較cyclosporine高） 感染 與cyclosporine相似 抗增殖藥物（Antiproliferative Agents） mycophenolate mofetil（黴酚酸酯，MMF） 作用機轉：抑制inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMPDH)，阻斷GMP合成，選擇性抑制T和B淋巴細胞增殖。
特性 說明 適應症 腎、心、肝移植；自體免疫疾病 給藥 口服或靜脈；每日2次 活性代謝物 Mycophenolic acid（MPA） 不良反應 系統 表現 胃腸道 腹瀉（最常見）；噁心、嘔吐 骨髓 白血球減少、血小板減少 感染 機會性感染（特別是CMV） azathioprine（硫唑嘌呤） 作用機轉：在體內轉化為6-mercaptopurine (6-MP)，干擾嘌呤合成，抑制淋巴細胞增殖。
特性 說明 適應症 腎移植；自體免疫疾病（類風濕關節炎、紅斑狼瘡） 給藥 口服或靜脈 不良反應 系統 表現 骨髓 劑量限制性骨髓抑制（特別是白血球減少） 肝臟 肝功能異常 胃腸道 噁心、嘔吐 注意：TPMT缺乏症患者禁用（會導致嚴重骨髓毒性）
mTOR抑制劑 sirolimus（ rapamycin，西羅莫司） 作用機轉：與FKBP-12結合，但不同於tacrolimus，此複合體抑制mTOR，阻斷細胞週期G₁至S期的進程，抑制T細胞增殖及血管平滑肌細胞增殖。
特性 說明 適應症 腎移植（與cyclosporine或tacrolimus合用）；心血管支架預防再狹窄 半衰期 長（約60-70小時） 不良反應 系統 表現 高脂血症 高膽固醇、高三酸甘油酯（常見） 傷口癒合延遲 移植術後傷口併發症 口腔潰瘍 口腔炎 肺部 間質性肺炎（少見但嚴重） 皮質類固醇（ Corticosteroids） 作用機轉：作為glucocorticoid receptor配體，進入細胞核調節基因轉錄；抑制NF-κB等轉錄因子，減少多種細胞激素（IL-1, IL-2, IL-6, TNF-α等）產生。
代表藥物 效能比較 Prednisone 中效；常用於維持治療 Methylprednisolone 強效；常用於靜脈脈衝治療 臨床應用 情境 說明 急性排斥反應 Methylprednisolone靜脈脈衝（500-1000 mg/d）×3天 移植維持免疫抑制 低劑量prednisone合併其他製劑 自體免疫疾病 SLE、血管炎、類風濕關節炎等 不良反應（長期使用） 系統 表現 代謝 高血糖、體重增加、脂肪分布異常（Cushing様） 骨骼 骨質疏鬆（預防：維生素D+鈣質補充） 免疫 感染風險增加 眼科 白內障、青光眼 心血管 高血壓、高血脂 抗發炎藥物 免疫抑制單株抗體 藥物 標的 適應症 說明 Basiliximab IL-2Rα (CD25) 腎移植 嵌合抗體；預防急性排斥 Daclizumab IL-2Rα 腎移植 （已停產） Alemtuzumab CD52 CLL、移植 去除T、B細胞；嚴重免疫抑制 Antithymocyte globulin (ATG) 多種T細胞抗原 急性排斥治療 動物（兔/馬）來源的抗淋巴細胞球蛋白 Rituximab CD20 B細胞淋巴瘤、移植 去除B細胞 免疫增強劑（Immunomodulators） 干擾素（Interferons） 類型 來源 主要作用 IFN-α 白血球 抗病毒；抗腫瘤（毛狀細胞白血病、B型肝炎、C型肝炎） IFN-β 成纖維細胞 抗病毒；多發性硬化症治療 IFN-γ T細胞、NK細胞 免疫調節；巨噬細胞活化 不良反應 系統 表現 流感様症狀 發燒、寒顫、肌肉酸痛（干擾素最常見） 神經 憂鬱（干擾素-α）；認知功能改變 骨髓 白血球減少、血小板減少 自體免疫 甲狀腺機能異常；自體抗體產生 自體免疫疾病治療藥物 疾病修飾抗風濕藥物（DMARDs） 藥物 作用機轉 主要適應症 Hydroxychloroquine 免疫調節 輕度類風濕、SLE Methotrexate 抗代謝（葉酸途徑） 類風濕關節炎、乾癬 Leflunomide 抑制pyrimidine合成 類風濕關節炎 Sulfasalazine 抗發炎、免疫調節 類風濕關節炎、發炎性腸病 Cyclosporine/Tacrolimus Calcineurin抑制 類風濕關節炎、乾癬 免疫抑制療法的臨床應用 器官移植免疫抑制方案 標準三合一療法（Triple Therapy）：
藥物 角色 Calcineurin抑制劑（cyclosporine或tacrolimus） 基礎免疫抑制 抗增殖藥物（MMF或azathioprine） 抑制淋巴細胞增殖 皮質類固醇（prednisone） 快速抗發炎/免疫抑制 急性排斥反應治療 等級 治療方式 細胞媒介（急性） 類固醇脈衝治療（Methylprednisolone 500-1000 mg/d×3天）或ATG 抗體媒介（急性） Rituximab或血漿置換 免疫抑制劑藥物交互作用 藥物組合 影響 Cyclosporine + Ketoconazole Ketoconazole抑制CYP3A4，增加cyclosporine濃度 Tacrolimus + Erythromycin 同上，增加tacrolimus濃度 Sirolimus + Cyclosporine 兩者協同腎毒性；需監測腎功能 MMF + Antacids 減少MMF吸收 免疫製劑過敏反應處理 ⚠️ 單株抗體靜脈注射可能引起輸注反應（infusion reactions）
反應程度 處理方式 輕度（瘙癢、皮疹） 減慢輸注速度；給予抗組織胺 中度（氣管痙攣） 停止輸注；皮質類固醇；腎上腺素 重度（過敏性休克） 立即腎上腺素注射；類固醇、抗組織胺 各類免疫抑制劑比較 藥物 主要作用點 腎毒性 神經毒性 代謝副作用 Cyclosporine T細胞（IL-2） 高 低 高血壓、高血鉀 Tacrolimus T細胞（IL-2） 高 高（顫抖） 新發生糖尿病 MMF T/B細胞增殖 無 無 腹瀉 Azathioprine T/B細胞增殖 無 無 骨髓抑制 Sirolimus mTOR 無 低 高血脂、傷口癒合延遲 Corticosteroids 廣泛抗發炎 高血壓、高血糖、骨質疏鬆
